newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call money eases a touch.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call money eases a touch.

text.p: Overnight guilder rates eased a touch on Wednesday in quiet trade as the market took a breather ahead of a flurry of end-of-year payments activity.
Dealers said a slight increase in market liquidity had enabled banks fractionally to increase their savings under the current secured loans pact running to January 17.

Call was quoted at an unchanged 2.81 percent bid towards the end of Wednesday's session after most deals had been done at around 2.81 and 2.87 percent, compared with Tuesday's 2.87 and 2.93 percent, dealers said.
Some dealers predicted a somewhat tighter allocation under the next special advances pact due on Friday in view of the Dutch finance ministry's repo activity.
Trade in longer-dated money was relatively slack, with one-year guilders easing a touch on swaps activity.
One-year guilders were quoted at 3.14 percent bid from Tuesday's 3.16 percent.
The guilder held steady against the mark at 112.17 guilders per 100 marks from Tuesday's 112.175 fixing.
